transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I really appreciate it. 

Um... I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of a hiccup at work. I'm a construction manager, and... well, it's probably not a huge deal, I really do try my best to stay on top of everything. But I've noticed that when I sit down for a safety briefing or a plan review, I'll be trying so hard to pay attention, and then within just a few minutes, my mind is completely off on three other job problems. 

Before I know it, I've missed things in the plans that I know I should have caught. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really want to do a good job and be reliable for my crew. Does that make sense? I just hope I'm not wasting your time with it.
Can you tell me if you've noticed this same kind of difficulty staying focused in other parts of your life, like at home or during conversations with friends or family?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try to be a good listener, especially for my wife, because she deserves that. But sometimes... well, my foreman or my wife will be talking straight to me, and I'm looking right at them, nodding, trying to be respectful. But then I realize I kind of spaced out, and I have to ask them, "Hey, sorry, could you run that by me again?" because I really only caught the last few words. 

I always feel terrible when it happens because I don't want them to think I don't care. I really do care. It's just... I get a little distracted sometimes, I suppose. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you ever feel unusually restless, as if you can't sit still for very long, or find yourself doing things without thinking them through first?

Um, restless? I mean... I don't know if I'd say *unusually* restless. I just like to stay busy, you know? In my line of work, you kind of have to be on your toes. 

But, well, I guess if I'm being completely honest... I do have a little trouble staying put sometimes. Like, if we have a sit-down meeting with the higher-ups or the architects... everybody else just sits there the whole time, taking notes. And I'm always the guy who's standing up, walking over to get a coffee, or stepping outside to "check on a delivery," or just making some excuse to move around a bit. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound unprofessional. I just... my legs get kind of antsy, and I feel like I think better when I'm moving. Is that okay? I mean, I always make sure the job gets done, I just don't do great sitting in one chair for an hour. Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I really don't think so. I'm actually a pretty upbeat guy, I promise! 

I love spending time with my wife and the kids, and I still really enjoy getting out to fish on the weekends when I can. I mean, sure, work gets a little stressful sometimes, but I don't feel hopeless or anything like that. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I wouldn't want to bring anybody down around me. 

I hope it's okay that I don't feel that way. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it normal that I don't feel sad like that?
Can you tell me if these problems with staying focused and feeling restless have been happening in places other than work, like at home, in social situations, or while doing personal tasks?

Well, um... I guess it does spill over a little bit. I really try to keep things running smooth everywhere, I promise I do. But... well, I suppose it's been a bit of an issue in both places lately. 

At work, I've been missing some follow-ups and... well, my site coordination hasn't been as tight as it usually is. It actually got to the point where my boss had to have a formal sit-down with me about it. I felt awful about that, because I always want to do a good job for them. 

And at home... I mean, I love my wife, and I really want to be helpful around the house. But I keep saying I'll handle things and then... I just kind of lose track of it. She's getting pretty worn down from having to remind me all the time. I hate being a burden to her, you know? 

I really hope I can get this sorted out so I can be better for both of them. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like a complete mess here.
Can you tell me if these problems with focus and restlessness have also happened in other situations, like when you're out with friends, running errands, or doing something by yourself?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really noticed it too much when I'm just out and about. I mean, I'm sure I have my moments, but I really try to be present when I'm with my buddies or out running errands for my wife. 

I guess maybe sometimes I might jump from one aisle to another at the hardware store without finishing what I was looking for, but... that's just because I remember something else we need, you know? I'm just trying to be efficient. And with friends, we're usually just shooting the breeze, so it's not like I have to sit still and take notes like at work. 

I hope that's okay. I really don't think it's a huge problem outside of work and the stuff at home I mentioned. Is it bad if it's mostly just those two places? I'm just trying to give you the clearest picture I can.
Have you noticed these same issues with losing focus or needing to move around when you're by yourself, like when you're reading, watching TV, or trying to relax after work?

Um, well... I mean, when I'm just by myself trying to relax, I don't really think it's too bad. I really try to just unwind, you know? I want to be able to just chill out after a long day. 

I guess maybe sometimes if I'm trying to watch a movie or something, I might get up to grab a drink or check on something in the garage... but I always come right back! It's just, you know, I like to stay productive, even when I'm off the clock. I don't think I'm, like, bouncing off the walls or anything when I'm alone. 

I hope that makes sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. It's totally fine if I just like to keep busy when I'm by myself, right?

Can you tell me if you've had trouble staying focused or feeling restless in situations like school, conversations, or when doing something that requires you to sit and pay attention for a while—like when watching a longer movie, attending a church service, or even during driver’s ed or training sessions?

Well, um... I guess when you put it like that, with training sessions or conversations... I mean, I try really hard to be professional and attentive, I promise. But... well, I suppose that's actually a big part of why I'm here. 

Like, if I'm running a safety briefing or reviewing a site plan... I go in with the best intentions. I tell myself, "Okay, focus up, this is important." But then... I don't know, within just a few minutes, it's like my brain just takes off. I start thinking about the concrete pour scheduled for tomorrow, or the framing crew running behind, and... before I know it, I've missed a detail in the plan that I know I should have caught. 

I feel terrible when it happens, because I really want to be the guy who has everything under control. I'm just trying to stay ahead of all the problems on the job site, you know? It's not that I don't care about the safety brief. I hope you don't think I'm just being careless. Does that sound like what you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Can you tell me if these difficulties with staying focused and feeling restless have been happening for a long time, maybe even going back to when you were in school as a child?

Well, um... I guess if we're going all the way back to school... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or anything. I was just, you know, a little energetic. I think a lot of boys are like that, right? 

But, um... yeah, I suppose my parents heard from my teachers a fair bit, even back in elementary school. They'd say things like I had trouble staying in my seat, or that I'd talk out of turn sometimes. And I guess I did lose my homework more than I should have. I always tried to do it, I just... couldn't always find it when it was time to turn it in. 

And sometimes I'd just kind of rush through the directions on an assignment before I really understood what I was supposed to do. I was just eager to get it done and move on to the next thing, you know? I really wasn't trying to be difficult or anything. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a troublemaker. Is that the kind of stuff you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Can you tell me if you've had similar issues with focus or restlessness during structured activities like church services, long movies, or community events where you're expected to sit and pay attention?

Um, well... I guess when it comes to those kinds of things, like long meetings or community events for a project... I try my absolute best to be respectful, I really do. But... yeah, I suppose I might have a little trouble just staying glued to the chair the entire time. 

Like, in these big sit-down meetings where everybody else can just sit through the whole thing without moving a muscle... I'm usually the guy standing up to grab another coffee, or I'll step outside for a second just to, you know, check on something real quick. I always try to do it quietly so I don't bother anyone! I just... I kind of end up making a little excuse to move around a bit. 

I just like to keep the blood flowing, you know? Being on a job site most of my life, my body's just used to being in motion. I hope that doesn't make me seem rude or unprofessional to the other guys. It's pretty normal to need to stretch your legs during a long sit-down, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something completely out of the ordinary here.
Can you tell me if these difficulties with focus and restlessness have caused you any significant problems in your job performance, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Well... um... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm failing at things, you know? I try so incredibly hard to be a good provider and a good husband. I really do. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has been causing some hiccups lately. 

At work, um... I guess I've missed a few follow-ups. Just little things, mostly, but... well, the site coordination hasn't been as smooth as it should be, and my boss actually sat me down to talk about it. It was just a formal concern, nothing too crazy, but... it felt awful. I hate letting them down when they trust me to run the site. 

And at home... I mean, my wife is wonderful, she really is. But I think she's getting a little... worn down. I'll tell her I'm going to handle something—like fixing a leaky pipe or paying a bill—and I really mean to do it! But then I just... forget. And she has to keep reminding me. I feel terrible about it because I want to be the guy she can rely on. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or a bad husband. I'm really trying my best to keep all the plates spinning. Is that the kind of information you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit.
Can you tell me if you've had trouble staying focused or feeling restless in situations like church services, long movies, or community events where you're expected to sit and pay attention?

Um, oh, I think we might have just talked about this a little bit, but, um... yeah, I guess those kinds of things are pretty similar to the meetings I was mentioning. 

Like I said, I really do try to be respectful when I'm supposed to be sitting still. But... yeah, if it's a long movie or a service or something where everyone else is just perfectly content sitting there for an hour or two without moving... I just, I really struggle to stay glued to the seat. 

I'll usually try to find a reason to get up, just for a second. Like, I'll be the guy who volunteers to go get the popcorn refills, or I'll step out to the lobby just to stretch my legs or check my phone real quick. I always try to do it at a part where I'm not blocking anyone's view or causing a distraction! I really hate being a bother to other people. 

I just... I kind of need to make an excuse to move around a little bit. It's just so hard for me to stay put when my body feels like it needs to be doing something. I hope that makes sense? I know I kind of repeated myself there, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about significant problems in job performance, relationships, or other important areas of life, which directly corresponds to the functional impairment caused by the symptoms.

patient.answer:
Well... um... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm failing at things, you know? I try so incredibly hard to be a good provider and a good husband. I really do. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has been causing some hiccups lately. 

At work, um... I guess I've missed a few follow-ups. Just little things, mostly, but... well, the site coordination hasn't been as smooth as it should be, and my boss actually sat me down to talk about it. It was just a formal concern, nothing too crazy, but... it felt awful. I hate letting them down when they trust me to run the site. 

And at home... I mean, my wife is wonderful, she really is. But I think she's getting a little... worn down. I'll tell her I'm going to handle something—like fixing a leaky pipe or paying a bill—and I really mean to do it! But then I just... forget. And she has to keep reminding me. I feel terrible about it because I want to be the guy she can rely on. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or a bad husband. I'm really trying my best to keep all the plates spinning. Is that the kind of information you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are present in multiple settings beyond work and home, which would support a diagnosis of ADHD (F90.0) over adjustment disorder (F43.20).
doctor.question: Can you tell me if you've had trouble staying focused or feeling restless in situations like church services, long movies, or community events where you're expected to sit and pay attention?

target_item.name: Leaving_Seat
target_item.manifestation: In meetings where everybody else can sit through the whole thing, I’m the guy standing up, walking to the coffee, stepping outside to check something, or making an excuse to move around.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about situations where I am expected to sit and pay attention, which directly corresponds to the symptom of leaving my seat when remaining seated is expected.

patient.answer:
Um, oh, I think we might have just talked about this a little bit, but, um... yeah, I guess those kinds of things are pretty similar to the meetings I was mentioning. 

Like I said, I really do try to be respectful when I'm supposed to be sitting still. But... yeah, if it's a long movie or a service or something where everyone else is just perfectly content sitting there for an hour or two without moving... I just, I really struggle to stay glued to the seat. 

I'll usually try to find a reason to get up, just for a second. Like, I'll be the guy who volunteers to go get the popcorn refills, or I'll step out to the lobby just to stretch my legs or check my phone real quick. I always try to do it at a part where I'm not blocking anyone's view or causing a distraction! I really hate being a bother to other people. 

I just... I kind of need to make an excuse to move around a little bit. It's just so hard for me to stay put when my body feels like it needs to be doing something. I hope that makes sense? I know I kind of repeated myself there, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of inattention and restlessness have been consistently reported across multiple settings (work, home, structured activities) and have been present since childhood. These difficulties are causing clinically significant impairment in social and occupational functioning, which aligns with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation (F90.0). There is no evidence supporting F43.20 (adjustment disorder with anxiety) given the chronic, lifelong pattern of symptoms rather than a reaction to a recent stressor.

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and determine the primary reason for the visit
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a persistent pattern of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity that began in childhood and continues into adulthood, causing functional impairment in both occupational and domestic settings. The symptoms are not better explained by a mood or anxiety disorder, and they meet the criteria for ADHD, predominantly combined presentation.
